relevant_points: SXS waveforms are affected by numerical truncation, finite-radius extraction, and extrapolation-related errors.
Mode mixing and center-of-mass corrections can affect subdominant modes, making mode-resolved error analyses scientifically meaningful.
The paper references an updated SXS catalog with 2018 simulations, consistent with catalog-scale quality assessments.
Higher harmonics such as (4,4) can require more careful modeling and can be substantially harder to capture accurately than dominant modes.
This motivates checking whether synthetic modal errors increase with harmonic index.
Surrogate waveform models are calibrated directly to numerical relativity simulations and require simulation errors to be at or below model error budgets.
The cited training set size of 1528 simulations is similar to the scale of the provided synthetic catalog summaries.
Accurate surrogate modeling for eccentric binary black holes depends on low waveform mismatches, typically around 1e-3 to 1e-2 in examples cited in the paper.
This provides context for interpreting the synthetic error levels in the provided datasets.

contract_updates: Preserve catalog-scale perspective rather than over-interpreting individual rows as full simulations.
Prioritize figures that compare overall resolution error, mode-by-mode error growth with l, and extrapolation-order disagreement.
Explicitly discuss implications for waveform-model calibration and truncation of higher-order modes.
